lesson.name: Lesson 13 · 전화
lesson.summary: Handle everyday phone calls, talk about illness, make polite requests, express obligations, promises, causes, and formal intention.
goals: Describe body pain and common illness
Ask someone to do something for you with -아/어 주다
Say what you have to do with -아/어야 되다
Give a noun-based reason with N 때문에
Use intentional -겠- in formal or fixed expressions
classFocus: Phone-call flow and polite telephone language

phoneFlow.label: Answer
phoneFlow.hint: Use this when answering the phone.

phoneFlow.label: Confirm / identify
phoneFlow.hint: Check that you reached the right person/place.

phoneFlow.label: Ask for someone
phoneFlow.hint: A polite way to ask to speak to someone.

vocabulary.meaning: for a moment / just a moment

grammar.title: Do something for someone
grammar.explain: Attach -아/어 주다 to a verb when an action is done for someone else's benefit. In requests, -아/어 주세요 is often more considerate than a plain command.
examples: 친구가 사진을 찍어 줬어요. — My friend took a picture for me.
전화번호를 가르쳐 주세요. — Please tell me your phone number.
기다려 주셔서 감사합니다. — Thank you for waiting for me.
grammar.contrast: -아/어 주세요 emphasizes a favor/benefit; -(으)세요 is a more direct polite command.

grammar.title: Have to / must
grammar.explain: Use this pattern for obligation or necessity. -아/어야 하다 is slightly more formal, while -아/어야 되다 is very common in conversation.
examples: 내일 일찍 일어나야 돼요. — I have to get up early tomorrow.
친구한테 전화해야 돼요. — I have to call my friend.
책을 빌려야 돼요. — I have to borrow a book.
grammar.contrast: 되다 and 하다 express the same core obligation here; style/register differs slightly.
grammar.pitfall: Remember the 아/어 conjugation before 야: 가다 → 가야, 먹다 → 먹어야, 하다 → 해야.

grammar.title: A promise or willingness for the listener
grammar.explain: Use -(으)ㄹ게요 when the speaker makes a promise, assurance, or listener-oriented decision. The subject is normally first person and it is not used as a question.
grammar.formula: consonant + 을게요 / vowel or ㄹ + ㄹ게요
examples: 제가 설거지할게요. — I'll do the dishes.
나중에 전화할게요. — I'll call you later.
책을 빌려줄게요. — I'll lend you the book.
grammar.contrast: -(으)ㄹ래요 can express a personal preference/intention and can appear in questions; -(으)ㄹ게요 is a promise/assurance and cannot be used as a question.
grammar.pitfall: Do not use third-person subjects such as 'Michael will...' with -(으)ㄹ게요.

grammar.title: Because of a noun
grammar.explain: Use 때문에 after a noun or noun phrase to give a cause or reason. In short answers, the rest of the sentence can be omitted when the context is clear.
examples: 비 때문에 길이 막혀요. — The road is congested because of the rain.
숙제 때문에 바빴어요. — I was busy because of homework.
감기 때문에 학교에 못 갔어요. — I couldn't go to school because of a cold.
grammar.contrast: -아/어서 connects clauses; 때문에 follows a noun/noun phrase.
grammar.pitfall: 때문에 is not normally used by itself; attach it to a noun phrase.

grammar.title: Formal intention / volition
grammar.explain: Intentional -겠- can mark the speaker's intention or volition, especially in formal speech and fixed expressions. In everyday speech, other endings such as -(으)ㄹ래요 may often sound more natural.
examples: 내일 다시 오겠습니다. — I will come again tomorrow.
수업을 시작하겠습니다. — We will begin the class.
잘 먹겠습니다. — Thank you for the food / I will eat well.
grammar.contrast: Conjectural -겠- means something like 'I guess / it must be'; intentional -겠- means 'I will'. Context decides which reading is intended.
grammar.pitfall: Do not combine intentional -겠- with a past-tense suffix.

practice.prompt: You answer a phone call. What is the most natural opening?
practice.why: 여보세요 is the standard telephone greeting.

practice.prompt: Choose the best polite way to ask to speak to 민수.
practice.why: 바꿔 주세요 is used to ask the person answering to pass/switch the phone.

practice.prompt: Translate: 'My head hurts.'
practice.why: Body part + 이/가 + 아파요 is the core pattern.

practice.prompt: Translate: 'My feet hurt.'
practice.why: 발 takes the subject particle 이.

practice.prompt: Which sentence means 'Please wait for me'?
practice.why: -아/어 주세요 asks someone to do an action for the speaker.

practice.prompt: Change 돕다 into the polite favor form: 'Please help me.'
practice.why: 돕다 is irregular here: 돕 + 아 → 도와.

practice.prompt: Which is more appropriate when politely asking someone to pass the phone to 민호?
practice.why: The favor form is the more appropriate request in this telephone context.

practice.prompt: Complete: 내일 일찍 ________. (I have to get up early tomorrow.)
practice.why: -아/어야 되다 expresses obligation.

practice.prompt: Translate: 'I have to do laundry.'
practice.why: 하다 → 해야 before 되다/하다.

practice.prompt: Which means 'I have to borrow a book'?
practice.why: 빌리다 → 빌려야 돼요.

practice.prompt: Which sentence is a listener-oriented promise?
practice.why: -(으)ㄹ게요 expresses the speaker's promise/assurance.

practice.prompt: Which sentence is NOT acceptable with -(으)ㄹ게요?
practice.why: The subject of -(으)ㄹ게요 is normally first person.

practice.prompt: Which can naturally be used as a question?
practice.why: -(으)ㄹ래요 can be used in questions; -(으)ㄹ게요 cannot.

practice.prompt: Choose the best way to say 'because of homework'.
practice.why: N 때문에 = because of N.

practice.prompt: Translate: 'I couldn't go to school because of a cold.'
practice.why: 감기 is a noun, so N 때문에 is appropriate.

practice.prompt: Which structure directly follows a noun phrase?
practice.why: 때문에 attaches to a noun/noun phrase; -아/어서 connects predicates/clauses.

practice.prompt: Choose the formal intentional sentence: 'We will begin the class.'
practice.why: Intentional -겠- is common in formal announcements and intentions.

practice.prompt: In '피곤하겠어요', what is the likely meaning of -겠-?
practice.why: Here -겠- is conjectural, not intentional; context distinguishes the two.

practice.prompt: The line is busy. Which expression fits?
practice.why: 통화중이에요 means the line/person is busy on another call.

practice.prompt: Write a natural short promise: 'I'll call you later.'
practice.why: This combines a phone expression with -(으)ㄹ게요.
